name: Adding a Bathroom to Your Home: Step-by-Step Construction Timeline

step.name: Step 1: Confirm layout dimensions and structural conditions
step.text: Measure the proposed space carefully to ensure adequate fixture clearances and verify that existing joists can support the extra floor weight. Have rough sketches ready showing door swings and fixture placements. Done looks like a clear, measured floor plan that respects code-required clearances.

step.name: Step 2: Secure necessary building, plumbing, and electrical permits
step.text: Submit your plans to the local building department before picking up tools or cutting framing. You will need approvals for altered walls, new electrical circuits, and added plumbing lines. Done means physical permit cards are posted on-site and approved plans are in hand.

step.name: Step 3: Rough-in the drain, vent, and water supply lines
step.text: Run drainpipes at proper slopes and install supply plumbing before any insulation or wallboard goes up. Ensure vent lines connect properly to prevent siphoning and sewer gas intrusion. Done looks like complete pipe rough-ins under test pressure, ready for city inspection.

step.name: Step 4: Install dedicated electrical wiring and exhaust ventilation
step.text: Pull new home runs for GFCI outlets and lighting, and route a dedicated exhaust fan ducted completely to the home exterior. Never vent moisture into attics or interior floor cavities. Done means all boxes, wiring, and exhaust ductwork terminate securely outdoors.

step.name: Step 5: Waterproof wet zones and hang moisture-resistant drywall
step.text: Install cementitious backer board in shower areas, apply liquid waterproofing membranes, and hang moisture-resistant drywall on surrounding surfaces. Inspect corners and seams for seamless waterproof coverage. Done looks like a fully sealed, flat substrate ready for tile and tape.

step.name: Step 6: Set tile, install fixtures, and apply finish paint
step.text: Lay floor and wall tile, set the vanity, hook up the toilet, install plumbing trim, and apply durable interior paint. Check every valve for leaks and ensure switches control the proper fixtures. Done is a fully operational, clean, and tested bathroom space. Ready to expand your living space?
